topic: Hermes Agent skill surfaces, external skill mounting, and agent-OS / skill-governance patterns (2026)
must_answer: What is Hermes Agent's official mechanism for mounting external skill directories?
What official self-evolution / skill-improvement surfaces exist for Hermes in 2026?
What recent research/surveys describe agent-skill architecture, security, and governance?
What product-level 'agent OS' framing appears in adjacent agent tooling discourse?

sources.title: Skills System | Hermes Agent
sources.excerpt: Add external_dirs under the skills section in ~/.hermes/config.yaml. Paths support ~ expansion and ${VAR} environment variable substitution. Existing skills are modified where they are found, including skills under external_dirs.

sources.title: NousResearch/hermes-agent-self-evolution
sources.excerpt: Hermes Agent Self-Evolution uses DSPy + GEPA (Genetic-Pareto Prompt Evolution) to automatically evolve and optimize Hermes Agent's skills, tool descriptions... Phase 1 Skill files (SKILL.md) DSPy + GEPA Implemented.

sources.title: Nous Research Adds /learn to Hermes Agent's Skills System
sources.excerpt: Nous Research adds /learn to Hermes Agent, authoring reusable SKILL.md files from directories, doc URLs, conversations, and pasted notes.

sources.title: Bundled Skills Catalog - Hermes Agent
sources.excerpt: Catalog of bundled skills including research/arxiv, blogwatcher, llm-wiki, polymarket under research category.

sources.title: Agent Skills for Large Language Models: Architecture, Acquisition, Deployment, and Security (v4)
sources.excerpt: Organizes agent skills along architectural foundations (SKILL.md), skill acquisition (SAGE, SEAgent), deployment, and security; reports 26.1% of community-contributed skills contain vulnerabilities; proposes Skill Trust and Lifecycle Governance Framework with four-tier gate-based permissions.

sources.title: A Deterministic Control Plane for LLM Coding Agents
sources.excerpt: Treats agent definitions as a managed supply chain (SHA-256 content addressing, HMAC-stamped lockfiles); handoff.md for delegation receipts; append-only hash-chained audit log.

sources.title: Build Agent Skills Faster with Claude Code 2.1 Release
sources.excerpt: Frames Claude Code 2.1 as transforming into a full-fledged agent operating system via skill hot-reload, lifecycle hooks, and forked sub-agents using Markdown + YAML.

sources.title: Abraxas ↔ Hermes OS Unification 001
sources.excerpt: Three-layer OS: Visual OS + Abraxas core/Alembic + Hermes Agent OS; signal acquisition as primary syscall via abx-familiar-signal-forager → EvidencePack.v0.
sources.retrieved_note: local OBSERVED repo artifact from this campaign

claims.text: Hermes mounts external skill trees via skills.external_dirs in config.yaml with ~ and ${VAR} expansion; skills under external_dirs are editable in place by skill_manage.
Official Hermes self-evolution surface hermes-agent-self-evolution uses DSPy + GEPA; Phase 1 targets SKILL.md evolution and is marked implemented.
Hermes ships a /learn command that authors SKILL.md from directories, docs, conversations, and notes without hand-writing the skill from scratch.
claims.confidence_note: Secondary coverage of Nous feature; treat as OBSERVED of press claim, verify against live docs if promoting

claims.text: Hermes maintains an official bundled skills catalog including research tools such as arxiv and polymarket.
A 2026 survey on agent skills proposes a Skill Trust and Lifecycle Governance Framework and reports 26.1% of community-contributed skills contain vulnerabilities.
Deterministic control-plane research for coding agents emphasizes content-addressed agent definitions, HMAC lockfiles, handoff receipts, and hash-chained audit logs.
Adjacent agent tooling discourse (Claude Code 2.1) explicitly markets skill hot-reload + hooks + forked sub-agents as an 'agent operating system'.
claims.confidence_note: Secondary Medium article; product marketing language

claims.text: Abraxas local OS unification doc defines Hermes as Agent OS layer with signal forage EvidencePack as the primary syscall into Abraxas core.
Governed skill ecosystems (external_dirs mount + SHADOW evolution + trust gates) are becoming a competitive dimension for agent runtimes, not just model quality.

answers.summary: skills.external_dirs in config.yaml; ~ and ${VAR} supported; external skills editable in place.
Official DSPy+GEPA self-evolution repo (Phase 1 SKILL.md); /learn skill authoring; bundled skills catalog.
Agent-skills survey (trust/governance + vulnerability rate) and deterministic control-plane paper (lockfiles/handoffs/audit).
Claude Code 2.1 'agent OS' marketing + Abraxas three-layer OS doc; control-plane paper supplies engineering substrate metaphors.
No public TAM/revenue figures grounded in this forage; refuse commercial sizing.
